topics.title: A bit of BmMT
topics.text:
Here is a BmMT problem that I'm having some trouble with. Can someone point out the flaws in my solution? The answer from the answer key is also provided.



[quote=2014 BmMT Individual #11]Alice, Bob, Clara, David, Eve, Fred, Greg, Harriet, and Isaac are on a committee. They need to split into three subcommittees of three people each. If no subcommittee can be all male

or all female, how many ways are there to do this?[/quote]



Answer$360$


Bogus SolutionWithout restrictions, there are $\binom{8}{2} \binom{5}{2} = 280$ ways to sort them into subcommittees, by looking from an arbitrary person's perspective and choosing his or her partners. (This is already smaller than the answer... strange?) Now, we consider three cases and perform PIE



Case 1: There exist an entirely female committee. This means that we choose three people from the four existing girls (Alice, Clara, Eve, Harriet) to form a committee, then sort the rest into committees. This has $\binom{4}{3} \binom{5}{2} = 40$ ways to do so.



Case 2: There exist an entirely male committee. This means that we choose three people from the five existing males (Bob, David, Fred, Greg, Isaac) and sort the rest. This has $\binom{5}{3} \binom{5}{2} = 100$ ways to do so.



Case 3: There exist an entirely male committee and an entire female committee. We choose three people from the four girls and three people from the five boys, and sort the remaining people into a single committee. This has $\binom{5}{3} \binom{4}{3} = 40$ ways.



By PIE, there are $40 + 100 - 40 = 100$ ways to do this. Thus, there are $280 - 100 = \boxed{180}$ committees that are satisfactory.



This can also be done by noting that when there is an entirely female committee, there will be an entirely male committee no matter what.
